title: This Spider Has No Ears. It Still Hears a Fly Six Feet Away
subject: ogre-faced spider

scenes.text: This spider has no ears. It still hears a fly six feet away.
It hangs upside down in the dark, holding a tiny net between its front legs.
Its huge eyes can't see a flying insect. Blinded spiders still caught flying prey.
The secret is in its legs. Sensors in the leg joints pick up the sound of a fly's wingbeats.
When the fly comes close, the spider backflips and throws the net in about two tenths of a second.
So that spider didn't see you coming. It heard you with its knees.

description:
The ogre-faced spider has no ears, yet it can hear flying insects from up to six feet away.
Sensors in its leg joints pick up wingbeats, and it backflips a net over its prey in about 0.2 seconds.
Would you want to hear with your legs?
